body:
```suggestion
	const T &interpolated() const { return _interp; }
```

I'm not a big fan of abbreviated names for functions :)

That would also be fine (and I can see that makes a lot of sense, and I'm not averse to sticking them there at least temporarily, they are pretty easy to relocate at this stage, so I can stick them there for now).

I remember being unsure the most appropriate place to put these longterm, and it wasn't cut and dry. Probably between:

* `InterpolatedProperty`
* `TransformInterpolator`
* `Math`

I admit there was some pre-empting here - I can foresee future demand for some kind of user mechanism to do the same from gdscript, or using these from other areas, in which case if these are in `InterpolatedProperty` we'll probably want to move them somewhere else more generic.

I did consider the alternative of putting them directly in `Math`, but was aware the advice is usually to localize solutions first, and _then_ consider making them more generic only when required. See [best practices for engine contributors](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/best_practices_for_engine_contributors.html#prefer-local-solutions) .

`TransformInterpolator` is currently just a way of conveniently grouping all the physics interpolation functions together at the moment (without a lot of dependencies), so they can be used from different call points (client, server, bound funcs). Some of the existing functionality is likely a little too specific to put in `Math`. The other divergence is that `Math` is intended to be generic, whereas `TransformInterpolator` is code to do a specific task fast (and there may be shortcuts in terms of error checking where done in advance).

Regarding lerp functions specifically, there is a general problem to solve here that they are mostly OOP functions in a bunch of the classes, like `Vector2` `Vector3` etc, but they are not standardized (especially in 3.x), and calling them from macros that don't care about the underlying class is not always easy / possible. This may well have come up before in 4.x too about gdscript, in the discussions about the bound free function `lerp` versus OOP functions.

I suspect in the longrun we may end up moving them (or similar) to `Math`, but more bikeshedding will be involved there and sometimes it can be nice to defer this until a generic need is required, as the guidelines say.

body:
Naming is always one of the most difficult problems in programming :grin: .. I've tried a few different names for this over the years but currently am tending towards `pump` or `fti_pump`. It essentially acts like a pump, on every tick you are moving current values over to previous values (it is also sometimes reused for reset, but resetting refers to the _intention_ in a specific circumstance, not the _mechanism_).

_(This is also why `teleport` is imo a better naming than `reset_physics_interpolation`, because it makes the intention clear, whereas `reset` is very vague and users often get confused about it.)_

This pump is the core of how fixed timestep interpolation works, it relies on maintaining a continuous flow of previous and current transforms / properties / whatever, and then interpolating between them using the interpolation fraction.

I'm happy to put some more comments in.

`snap_to_current_value` / `jump_to_current_value` I'm not sure describe what is going on, I for one have no idea what they are referring to (and I've been using FTI for 25 years lol :grin: ).

body:
Actually thinking about it, it may be possible to use `fti_tick()` here, let me have a look through.

Hmm, not absolutely sure tick is an improvement, as `fti_pump()` is also used for resets, and not just ticking, so in exchange for a more familiar name we would be introducing an element of confusion. What happens if we start requiring users / contributors to call `tick()` outside of ticks?

I'm tending towards preferring sticking with bespoke terminology for physics interpolation, because in retrospect I think Juan fell into the same trap here with this desire to use "familiar" words:

* "FTI" became "physics interpolation" - caused confusion because it is nothing to do with physics
* "teleport" became "reset physics interpolation" - again users have no idea what this does or when to use

I think the way to follow the guideline would be to put them in `InterpolatedProperty`, not some other class which is currently dedicated specifically to transforms. I understand that in the future this lerp code and the TransformInterpolator code could be put together somewhere with bindings, but imho it makes more sense to move things around (and rename the class) then instead of now. There could be a TODO comment about this unification (and possibly binding). Anyway, I'll leave it up to you.
